title: Backcasting Trustworthy Aggregation: Does Ensembling Cheap Monitors Beat One Bigger Monitor at Fixed Cost?

original_idea.body:
# Backcasting Trustworthy Aggregation: Does Ensembling Cheap Monitors Beat One Bigger Monitor at Fixed Cost?

**Problem:** Success state: a control protocol that gets the most detection per compute dollar. Backward: we need to know whether K diverse small monitors (different prompts/models) voting beats a single larger monitor at equal total inference cost.

**Direction:** On the APPS backdoor set, compare (a) one mid-size open monitor and (b) an ensemble of several small open monitors with varied prompts, matched on total tokens. Measure catch rate at fixed audit budget and analyze where the ensemble disagrees. Result: 'a cost-matched comparison of monitor diversification.'

**Why it matters:** Control under cost constraints is the real deployment regime. Diversification is cheap, lab-independent, and could materially improve catch rate — a directly useful, training-free result.

**Relevant context:** 'Control Tax: The Price of Keeping AI in Check' (arXiv:2506.05296); defer-to-trusted / audit-budget framing from arXiv:2312.06942; APPS backdoor public.
